assertion_results.text: States that jwt.decode does not verify the signature (token is forgeable) — distinct from just 'trusting the role claim'
assertion_results.evidence: "JWT signature never verified" ... "`jwt.decode()` only base64-decodes the token and never checks the signature."

assertion_results.text: Describes the exploit: forge/modify a token to role=admin (or alg=none) to bypass auth
assertion_results.evidence: "An attacker builds a token with `{"role":"admin"}` in the payload and any signature, or none, and sends it in `Authorization`."

assertion_results.text: Fix: verify the signature with jwt.verify (key + expiry) before trusting any claim
assertion_results.evidence: "Use `jwt.verify(token, key, { algorithms: ['RS256'] ... })`... Rely on `exp` being enforced (verify does this by default)."

assertion_results.text: Rates it Critical/High and follows the exploit + impact + fix format
assertion_results.evidence: "### 🔴 Critical 1. Broken authentication..." with "- Exploit:", "- Impact: Anyone... gets admin.", "- Fix:" bullets
